column5: Look: modern kids' cartoon with Vietnamese motifs: soft, rounded, bright figures; warm
References: none from Luan (he skipped the taste questions). Values only from the genre
View: 2D · Camera: side view, follows the hero; locks at each fight until the group is gone,
Side-scrolling mission with stop-and-go fights, 4 beats read from `MISSION.beats` (3 or 4 work)
Move / attack / hold-to-defend, touch-first thumb pads + keyboard mirror, multi-touch
3 enemy kinds, each with its own silhouette: spear soldier, shield soldier, leader
Telegraphed attacks (glow + "!"), defend always blocks when held
Non-violent knock-back: bounce, star burst, drum; the last hit drops the weapon and they run
First-time hand hints on move, attack and defend; a pulse hint after 5 s with no progress
Intro panel, beat captions and ending line, all ⟨placeholder⟩, one short sentence each
Quiz: 4 questions by default (3–5 in config), 3 picture answers each, retry on wrong
Stars (quiz only) and an unlock screen for the next hero ⟨placeholder⟩
VI default, EN switch on every screen, remembered in localStorage; bundled Nunito font
Pause, mute, and a "turn your phone sideways" overlay in portrait
Title: tap **Bắt đầu**.
One picture panel with one short ⟨placeholder⟩ sentence, tap **Tiếp**.
A pointing hand bobs on ▶; the child holds it and the hero walks through a village.
The screen stops, a soldier walks in, the hand moves to Attack; one tap swings the staff and knocks him back with a drum hit and a burst of stars.
When a soldier glows yellow with a "!", the hand moves to Defend; holding it blocks with a clang.
After two hits he drops his spear and runs off, and a one-line ⟨placeholder beat 1⟩ caption ends the beat.
The first real trouble is beat 2 (about minute 2): two soldiers at once, one of them a shield soldier who takes three hits.
Beat 3 sends one from behind.
Beat 4 has the leader, bigger and slower, five hits.
Telegraphs are 1.1 s, so watching and defending is the skill.
A missed block only pushes the hero back a little; nothing is lost and there is no game over.
Stars come from the quiz alone: 3 for no wrong answers, 2 for up to two, 1 for finishing.
